criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: All required elements (rationale, primary objective, single vs constellation trade-off, operator, and multiple distinct customers) are clearly addressed and supported by credible literature.

evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS), which already runs the long-term monitoring program
The customers are the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority, which uses bleaching maps to direct in-water surveys

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Exceptional technical depth across all prompt topics: analytical derivations (azimuth, nodal precession rate, decay rates, data budgets), comprehensive orbital elements, ground station contact analysis, and software integration (STK screenshots and file listing).

evidence.quote: The baseline is an SSMS rideshare flight on Vega C from Kourou in early 2025
The Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory near Hobart, Tasmania (42.8°S, 147.4°E) is selected.
With a 4 m² sail the satellite re-enters about two years after the end of the mission.

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: The conclusion thoroughly synthesises the main findings and metrics while providing an outstanding, candid appraisal of technical limitations and future design steps.

evidence.quote: The design has four limitations. First, Vega C has not yet flown... Second, fluid lensing has only been demonstrated from aircraft

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Exemplary report formatting, logical progression, professional academic writing, clearly captioned tables/figures, and an appropriate IEEE-style bibliography matched seamlessly in-text.

evidence.quote: This report presents the design of ZYZZsat (Z-axis/Y-axis Zeroed Zoning Satellite), a single Earth observation microsatellite
[11] D. A. Vallado, Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications, 4th ed.

requirements.where: Appendix A: STK files and settings

overall: Outstanding submission demonstrating rigorous engineering design, flawless analytical hand calculations, appropriate software simulation, and exceptional critical reflection.

feedback.summary: You delivered an outstanding, professional engineering report that achieved full marks across all criteria. Your mission rationale, rigorous analytical calculations, software integration, and critical evaluations were exemplary.
next_steps: Apply this rigorous combination of hand calculations and software simulations to future complex orbital trade studies.
Maintain your practice of incorporating honest critical appraisals of technical limitations in future project conclusions.
Leverage your high standard of technical writing and professional report formatting in your upcoming engineering projects.

criteria.C1: You achieved the Accomplished level by clearly establishing ZYZZsat's mission rationale, constellation trade-off, operator, and customers with strong literature citations in Section 1.
criteria.C2: You reached the Accomplished level through exceptional analytical rigor in Sections 2.2–2.5, seamlessly combining analytical derivations with STK simulations and comprehensive subsystem planning.
criteria.C3: You met the Accomplished level in Section 3 by synthesizing your key metrics alongside a candid, detailed evaluation of technical limitations and necessary next steps.
criteria.C4: You satisfied the Accomplished standard with a logical structure, professional tone, polished figures, a clear executive summary, and properly integrated IEEE references.
